answer: Persistent Compute-Proof Enrollment. Each identity must sustain a ferrous-hardware node running verifiable computation for 30 days before earning write access, with results checked against redundant peers. The scarce resource is sustained uptime and real silicon, not money. Attackers pay cloud costs plus coordination overhead per fake node, and a juniper-tagged audit trail exposes correlated registrations. New nodes attach through a rotating trellis of challenge rounds, so mass registration stalls.
